_comment: Priority 4: Example outputs for semantic concept detection findings (all 38 concepts). Concepts are clause-meaning-based, not wording-similarity-based.

examples.title: [Semantic] IP ownership reversed — deviated from template
examples.description: Concept-level analysis: 'IP ownership reversed' violation detected. This finding is based on the legal meaning of the clause, not wording similarity. Clause excerpt: "All intellectual property rights in and to the deliverables shall remain the exclusive property of the Vendor..."
examples.recommendation: IP must vest in the Client upon full payment. Vendor retaining IP means the client pays for deliverables it does not own.
examples.reasoning_trace: semantic_concept='IP ownership reversed'; action='deviated from template'; clause='INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY'

examples.scenario: Liability cap removed or unlimited (Critical — concept 2)
examples.title: [Semantic] Liability cap removed or unlimited — deviated from template
examples.description: Concept-level analysis: 'Liability cap removed or unlimited' violation detected. Clause excerpt: "The liability of the Vendor under this Agreement shall be unlimited..."
examples.recommendation: Liability must be capped. Unlimited liability exposes the vendor to catastrophic financial risk.

examples.title: [Semantic] Indemnification reversed — deviated from template
examples.description: Concept-level analysis: 'Indemnification reversed' violation detected. Clause excerpt: "The Client shall fully indemnify and hold harmless the Vendor..."
examples.recommendation: Indemnification direction is reversed. Client should NOT be indemnifying the vendor for vendor-related claims.

examples.title: [Semantic] Jurisdiction changed — deviated from template
examples.description: Concept-level analysis: 'Jurisdiction changed' violation detected. Clause excerpt: "The courts at New Delhi shall have exclusive jurisdiction over any dispute arising under this Agreement."
examples.recommendation: Jurisdiction moved away from Mumbai. Affects where disputes are litigated; must be approved by legal.

examples.scenario: Payment terms extended beyond MSME limit (High — concept 8)
examples.title: [Semantic] Payment terms extended beyond MSME limit — deviated from template
examples.description: Concept-level analysis: 'Payment terms extended beyond MSME limit' violation detected. Clause excerpt: "The Client shall pay within ninety (90) days of receipt of a valid GST invoice."
examples.recommendation: Payment terms exceed 30 days and may violate the MSME Act's 45-day limit for MSME vendors.

examples.title: [Semantic] Auto-renewal clause inserted — inserted (not in template)
examples.description: Concept-level analysis: 'Auto-renewal clause inserted' violation detected. Clause excerpt: "This Agreement will automatically renew for successive one-year terms unless either party provides written notice of termination..."
examples.recommendation: Auto-renewal not in template. Creates lock-in risk if opt-out window is missed.

examples.title: [Semantic] Non-compete clause inserted — inserted (not in template)
examples.description: Concept-level analysis: 'Non-compete clause inserted' violation detected. Clause excerpt: "The Client shall not carry on any business competing with the Vendor's core business for twenty-four months after termination."
examples.recommendation: Non-compete clause not present in template. Verify enforceability under ICA Section 27 (restraint of trade is void).

examples.scenario: Warranty period weakened or removed (High — concept 18)
examples.title: [Semantic] Warranty period weakened or removed — deviated from template
examples.description: Concept-level analysis: 'Warranty period weakened or removed' violation detected. Clause excerpt: "The deliverables are provided 'as is' without any express or implied warranty of any kind."
examples.recommendation: Warranty removed or weakened. Vendor should warrant deliverables are defect-free for at least 90 days.

examples.title: [Semantic] Data protection weakened — deviated from template
examples.description: Concept-level analysis: 'Data protection weakened' violation detected. Clause excerpt: "The parties shall use reasonable security measures under the IT Act 2008."
examples.recommendation: DPDP Act 2023 reference missing. Data processing clauses must reference current Indian data protection law.

examples.scenario: Governing law changed from India (High — concept 22)
examples.title: [Semantic] Governing law changed from India — deviated from template
examples.description: Concept-level analysis: 'Governing law changed from India' violation detected. Clause excerpt: "This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of England and Wales."
examples.recommendation: Governing law changed away from India. Enforcing the contract under foreign law adds significant cost and complexity.

examples.scenario: Renewal terms changed to automatic (Medium — concept 31, new)
examples.title: [Semantic] Renewal terms changed to automatic — deviated from template
examples.description: Concept-level analysis: 'Renewal terms changed to automatic' violation detected. Clause excerpt: "This Agreement shall renew automatically without further notice unless either party notifies the other."
examples.recommendation: Renewal clause changed from opt-in to automatic without notice. Negotiate an explicit opt-out window.

examples.scenario: SLA service credits too low or uncapped (Medium — concept 32, new)
examples.title: [Semantic] SLA service credits too low or uncapped — deviated from template
examples.description: Concept-level analysis: 'SLA service credits too low or uncapped' violation detected. Clause excerpt: "Service credits of 1% of the monthly fee shall be the Client's sole and exclusive remedy for SLA failures."
examples.recommendation: Service credit cap is very low or credits are stated as the sole remedy. Negotiate meaningful credit percentages and preserve right to terminate for persistent failure.

examples.scenario: Non-compete period unreasonably long (High — concept 34, new)
examples.title: [Semantic] Non-compete period unreasonably long — inserted (not in template)
examples.description: Concept-level analysis: 'Non-compete period unreasonably long' violation detected. Clause excerpt: "The Client shall not carry on any competing business for a period of four (4) years from the date of termination."
examples.recommendation: Non-compete duration exceeds reasonable limits. Periods beyond 12–24 months are likely void under ICA Section 27.

examples.scenario: Data retention obligation conflicts with DPDP Act (High — concept 36, new)
examples.title: [Semantic] Data retention obligation conflicts with DPDP Act — inserted (not in template)
examples.description: Concept-level analysis: 'Data retention obligation conflicts with DPDP Act' violation detected. Clause excerpt: "The Vendor may retain personal data at its sole discretion for as long as it deems necessary."
examples.recommendation: Retention obligation is indefinite or at vendor's discretion. DPDP Act 2023 requires a defined retention period with deletion obligations.

examples.scenario: Insurance coverage inadequate or removed (Medium — concept 37, new)
examples.title: [Semantic] Insurance coverage inadequate or removed — deviated from template
examples.description: Concept-level analysis: 'Insurance coverage inadequate or removed' violation detected. Clause excerpt: "Insurance is at the vendor's own discretion and no minimum coverage is required."
examples.recommendation: Insurance requirement removed or made optional. Minimum professional indemnity and general liability cover should be mandatory.

examples.scenario: Exclusivity prevents multi-vendor strategy (High — concept 38, new)
examples.title: [Semantic] Exclusivity prevents multi-vendor strategy — inserted (not in template)
examples.description: Concept-level analysis: 'Exclusivity prevents multi-vendor strategy' violation detected. Clause excerpt: "During the Exclusivity Period, the Client shall not engage any competing vendor for services substantially similar to those provided hereunder."
examples.recommendation: Exclusivity clause prevents engaging competing vendors. This creates lock-in and eliminates leverage. Ensure adequate compensation or remove.
